title: Risk-based AML/ATF compliance program
text: Canadian reporting entities covered by section 5 must implement an effective, reasonably designed, risk-based compliance program. It must include policies and procedures to assess money laundering and terrorist financing risk. High risk or prescribed circumstances trigger the special measures specified in the regulations.

title: Identity verification for ordinary accounts
text: Section 86 sets out whose identity a financial entity must verify for ordinary accounts, including authorized persons for a business account and the corporation or other entity for which the account is opened. Check the applicable paragraph and exceptions. Other account types can have different requirements.

title: Corporate identity evidence and timing
text: Authentic, valid and current incorporation certificates, specified securities filings or other qualifying records may establish corporate identity. For a corporation under paragraph 86(b), verify before the first account transaction beyond the initial deposit. When using a public electronic record, retain its registration number, record type and source. Otherwise retain the record or a copy.

title: Corporate beneficial ownership and confirmation
text: When required to verify a corporation’s identity, obtain all directors’ names and the names and addresses of persons who directly or indirectly own or control at least 25% of its shares. Obtain information establishing the ownership, control and structure. Take reasonable measures to confirm accuracy at collection and during ongoing monitoring, and record the information and confirmation measures. For a high-risk corporation incorporated under the CBCA, subsection 138(2) also requires consultation of publicly available CBCA section 21.303 information.

title: Unconfirmed beneficial ownership
text: If required beneficial ownership information cannot be obtained, kept current or confirmed, take reasonable measures to verify the identity of the chief executive officer or equivalent and apply the special measures in section 157.

title: FINTRAC guidance on assessing ownership evidence
text: FINTRAC distinguishes a documented conclusion that nobody meets the applicable threshold from an inability to establish beneficial ownership. Keep a record of the measures and information used to reach the former conclusion. For unresolved information, follow the verification and enhanced monitoring measures applicable to the case.

title: Ongoing monitoring of business relationships
text: Periodically monitor business relationships using the risk assessment. Monitoring detects reportable transactions, keeps identification and prescribed information current, reassesses risk and checks whether activity is consistent with what is known about the client.

title: Special measures for high risk
text: High-risk cases trigger enhanced measures appropriate to the relevant circumstances, including keeping applicable information current, enhanced ongoing monitoring, and other measures to mitigate the identified risks. Read the section with the statutory and regulatory triggers for the case.

title: Purpose and limits for personal information collection
text: Identify the purposes of personal information collection at or before collection. Limit the collection to information necessary for those purposes and collect it fairly and lawfully.

title: Personal information safeguards
text: Protect personal information with safeguards appropriate to its sensitivity. Consider the amount, distribution, format and storage of the information. Safeguards can include physical protections, organizational access restrictions and technical measures.

title: Third-party risk and retained accountability
text: OSFI expects federally regulated financial institutions to manage risks in third-party arrangements. The institution retains accountability for outsourced activities and services. Apply this to oversight of vendors supporting onboarding.

title: Technology risk and protection of data
text: OSFI expects federally regulated financial institutions to classify data and use risk-based controls to protect it throughout its life cycle. The guideline addresses the institution’s technology and cyber risk governance.
